name: Chisel
text: Creative owns the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript merge with a 10-minute Engineering review *only if* they deliver a *live* timestamped draft within 24 hours—no static spec, no upfront debates. This forces Creative to commit to a working draft fast, letting Engineering catch obvious gaps (e.g., missing speaker labels) before the transcript stabilizes. The trade-off is accepting imperfect metadata early, but it beats waiting for a perfect spec that never ships.

name: Sift
text: Creative’s one-page spec is shelfware bait—it forces Creative to predict edge cases they can’t know upfront. Engineering’s live 10-minute ingest review is the real fix: it catches errors *as they happen*, not after the transcript evolves. Done-criteria: Engineering owns the checklist and runs the review before Creative merges.

name: Scope
text: Creative owns a *live* 10-minute ingest review for the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript, run by Engineering, using a shared checklist they co-author on the spot. This forces real-time fixes instead of debating a static spec, cutting the risk of misattributed sleep science claims while keeping the launch on track. The trade-off is that Engineering must drop other work for 10 minutes, but that’s cheaper than a week of delays or a broken AI Assistant.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Reel’s one-page spec and Engineering’s 10-minute review both treat the transcript as a static artifact, but the real risk is that the *Science of Sleep Optimization* launch stalls because Creative and Engineering keep reopening the spec when the transcript changes. The single best improvement is for Creative to own a *living* metadata spec—one they update in real time as the transcript evolves—and for Engineering to own a *5-minute* automated pre-merge check that flags missing fields or timestamps *before* Creative even submits it. That settles the argument: Creative controls the spec’s accuracy, Engineering enforces it instantly, and the transcript never becomes shelfware.

name: Reel
text: Creative owns the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript merge *immediately*, using a *live* 10-minute Engineering ingest review to flag missing fields or timestamps *before* the transcript hits the AI Assistant. This trades the risk of a one-off spec becoming shelfware for the certainty of catching errors in real time—no static document, no week-long debate. Engineering’s review is the bottleneck, but it’s short and prevents a broken AI Assistant. Done when the merged transcript is in the AI Executive Assistant pattern.

name: Scriv
text: Creative’s one-page spec won’t prevent misattributed sleep science claims—it’s a static snapshot of a moving transcript. Engineering’s live 10-minute ingest review catches errors *after* the damage is done. The real fix: Creative owns a *real-time* transcription pipeline with timestamped speaker labels, and Engineering owns a *one-click* validation rule to reject transcripts with gaps longer than 30 seconds before they’re merged. Done-criteria: the pipeline exists and the rule is enforced.
